messages.subject: Re: Advise on group comparison matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

the issue column in groupComparison outputs indicates if there was a problem with fitting a model for comparing groups. In your data, there is a lot of messages indicating that there are no measurements for one of the groups or both groups. In these cases, there is nothing to compare, so no p-value is produced. This could be either a data problem (too much missigness) or a problem with annotation. Is your annotation file correct? Follow-up question based on your script: does MSFragger indicates censored values by 0? If so, you should use the option censoredInt = "0" in dataProcess.

Kind regards
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT
messages.body_plain:
Hi Xuan,

For the BioReplicate column in the annotation file, each animal should have a unique ID. So either animal 1 or animal ID works as long as they are different for different animals.

For the normalization method, MSstatsTMT does not select a subset of proteins to normalize. Global median normalization (global_norm) performs normalization on peptide level data using all the proteins. Reference channel-based normalization (reference_norm) performs normalization on protein level data for each protein separately. More information can be found in manuscript: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8015007/pdf/main.pdf

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: Differential analysis question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ting

Thank you for looking into this. We've used 3 replicates per group (HEK only, Ecoli spiked in HEK (1:10 (w/w)), Ecoli spiked in HEK (1:20 (w/w))). The expected ratio of Ecoli protein regulation is 2x. Since all Ecoli proteins are expected to be regulated by a factor of 2 we would expect a higher number of significantly regulated with smaller adj.pvalues, as currently observed (similar to the SafeQuant volcano plot in my last post).

                                 ECHigh   ECLow
                    # runs     3             3
     # bioreplicates     3             3
 # tech. replicates    1              1

The script I've used:
library(MSstats) #v4.0.0
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

DDinput <- read.csv("DIA-30min_direcDIA_Report_organism.csv")

#convert Spectronaut format to MSstats format
DDraw <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(DDinput,
                                    annotation = NULL,
                                    intensity = 'PeakArea',
                                    filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
                                    qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
                                    useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
                                    fewMeasurements="remove",
                                    removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
                                    summaryforMultipleRows=max)

DDQuantData <- dataProcess(DDraw,
                           normalization='equalizeMedians',
                           summaryMethod="TMP",
                           censoredInt="0",
                           MBimpute=TRUE,

comparison <- MSstatsContrastMatrix("pairwise", c('High Ecoli', 'Low Ecoli', 'HEK'))
DDpairwiseComparison <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix=comparison, data=DDQuantData)

#add species information
DD_pwcomp <- with(DDpairwiseComparison,ComparisonResult)
DD_pwcomp$species <- DDinput$PG.Organisms[match(DD_pwcomp$Protein, DDinput$PG.ProteinGroups)]
DD_pwcomp <- DD_pwcomp %>% mutate(species = ifelse(grepl("Escherichia", species),"ecoli", ifelse(grepl("Homo", species),"human","unknown")))

#volcano plot
DD_pwcomp %>% filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(Protein),Label == "High Ecoli vs Low Ecoli") %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=log2FC, y=-log10(adj.pvalue), col=species)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-8,4),breaks=c(-8, -4, 0, 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,7),breaks=c(0, 2, 4, 6)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("High Ecoli vs Low Ecoli (MSstats)") +
  geom_vline(xintercept=c(-1, 1), col="red", linetype="dotted") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=-log10(0.05), col="red", linetype="dotted")

I'm also happy to share the dataset on which this analysis is based in case this is of any help...

Thank you already in advance for your help!

Kind regards,
Christian

messages.subject: Re: How to deal with missing values for differential expression analysis
messages.subject_clean: How to deal with missing values for differential expression analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

there are two kinds of missing values:
- missing at random (these are removed during summarization)
- missing due to low abundance - these are imputed at the feature level via accelerated failure time model.
You can control the missing values treatment via censoredInt, MBimpute and maxQuantileforCensored  parameters to dataProcess.

Kind regards
Mateusz
